title: Practice mix: pick the right test
idea: GUIDED review. Across several tiny problems, choose the comparison and branch that solve each - reinforcing the UEPCC habit.
problem: Small decision problems: pick the correct comparison and predict the one-choice result.

exercises.prompt: A problem outputs 'Adult' when age is 18 or more, else 'Minor'. The OUTPUT is...
exercises.explanation: One of two labels. Naming the output is always step one.
>= 18 includes 18 itself. 'or more' tells you to include the boundary.

exercises.prompt: By hand: age = 18 should give which label (rule: 18+ is Adult)?
exercises.explanation: 18 is '18 or more', so Adult. Edge values decide between > and >=.

exercises.prompt: A problem outputs 'In stock' only when count is above 0. Which test?
exercises.explanation: 'Above 0' is > 0. Note >= 0 would wrongly say 0 items are in stock.
0 > 0 is False, so the else runs: Sold out. Exactly the reason > (not >=) was chosen.

exercises.prompt: A problem outputs 'Match' when a code equals 1234. Which test?
exercises.explanation: Equality is ==. A single = would assign and break the condition.

exercises.prompt: Order the UEPCC steps you follow for any one-choice problem.
blocks: Plan: choose the comparison and branches
exercises.explanation: Understand, Example, Plan, Code, Check - the spine of every problem you will solve.
20 >= 25 is False, so the else runs: Cool.

exercises.prompt: Working an example by hand before coding gives you the value to check the code against.
exercises.explanation: Yes - the hand example is your answer key. Without it you cannot tell if the code is right.

exercises.prompt: The single most important first question for any problem is...
options: What is the output I must produce?
exercises.explanation: Start by naming the output. Everything else - inputs, plan, code, check - follows from knowing what you must produce.
